headline: An AsiaOne reader poll found that about one in five respondents who struggle with their mental health would talk to an AI chatbot about it.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the headline says people already do it, but this was a self-selected reader poll of 1,007 people about what they would do, not a national survey.
importance_line: It suggests some people in Singapore who struggle with their mental health would turn to chatbots, which a psychologist warns can give wrong advice and create dependency, but this was a self-selected reader poll about intentions, not actual use.
summary: AsiaOne reports that in its own audience poll of 1,007 readers, 20 per cent of those who struggle with mental health said they would talk to an AI chatbot about it, making it the fourth most chosen option after close friends, a mental health professional and a spouse. A clinical psychologist quoted warns that chatbots can give wrong information or encourage unhelpful thinking.
notes: Full AsiaOne text read. The poll is AsiaOne's own, run 15 May to 18 Jun 2026, and not representative of all Singaporeans.
